VIII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=8|verse=14}} And they forgot to take bread: and they had but one loafe vvith them in the boate. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}} And he commaunded them, {{ls}}aying, Looke vvel and bevvare of the leauen of the Phari{{ls}}ees, and the leauen of Herod. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}} And they rea{{ls}}oned among them {{ls}}elues {{ls}}aying, Becau{{ls}}e vve haue not bread. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}} Which {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving, {{ls}}aith to them, Why doe you rea{{ls}}on, becau{{ls}}e you haue not bread? do you not yet knovv nor vnder{{ls}}tand? yet haue ye your hart blinded? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}} hauing eies {{ls}}ee you not? and hauing eares heare you not? Neither do you remember? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}} When {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 6, 38.''}}* I brake fiue loaues among fiue thou{{ls}}and: and hovv many ba{{ls}}kets ful of fragmēts tooke you vp? They {{ls}}ay to him, Tvvelue. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 8, 5.''}}* When al{{ls}}o {{ls}}euen loaues among foure thou{{ls}}and, hovv many maundes of fragments tooke you vp? And they {{ls}}ay to him, Seuen. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=21}} And he {{ls}}aid to them, Hovv do you not yet vnder{{ls}}tand?

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=22}} And they come to Beth{{ls}}aida: and they bring to him one blinde, and de{{ls}}ired him that he vvould {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Our Sauiour v{{ls}}ed to worke much by touching: that we may learne not to cōtemne the corporal and external application of holy things, nor to chalēge by the {{ls}}pirit and faith only, as Heretikes doe.}}∷ touche him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=23}} And taking the hand of the blinde, he led him forth out of the tovvne: and {{ls}}pitting into his eies, impo{{ls}}ing his hands, he a{{ls}}ked him if he {{ls}}avv any thing. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=24}} And looking vp, he {{ls}}aid, I {{ls}}ee men as it vvere trees, vvalking. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=25}} After that againe he impo{{ls}}ed his hands vpon his eies, and be began to {{ls}}ee, and vvas re{{ls}}tored, {{ls}}o that he {{ls}}avv al things clerely. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=26}} And he {{ls}}ent him into his hou{{ls}}e, {{ls}}aying, Goe into thy hou{{ls}}e: and if thou enter in to the tovvne, tel no body.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=27}} And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 16, 13. Lu. 9, 18.''}}* {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent forth and his Di{{ls}}ciples into the tovvnes of Caesarêa-Philippi: and in the vvay he a{{ls}}ked his Di{{ls}}ciples, {{ls}}aying to them, Whom do men {{ls}}ay that I am? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=28}} Who an{{ls}}vvered him, {{ls}}aying, Iohn the Bapti{{ls}}t, {{ls}}ome Elias, & other {{ls}}ome as it vvere one of the Prophets. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=29}} Then he {{ls}}aith to them, But vvhom do you {{ls}}ay that I am? Peter an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid to him, Thou art Chri{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=30}} And he threatened them that they {{ls}}hould not tel any man of him.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=31}} And he began to teache them, that the Sonne of man mu{{ls}}t {{ls}}uffer many things, and be reiected of the Auncients and of the high Prie{{ls}}tes and the Scribes, and be killed: and after three daies ri{{ls}}e againe. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=32}} And he {{ls}}pake the vvord openly. And Peter taking him, began to rebuke him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=33}} Who turning, and {{ls}}eeing his Di{{ls}}ciples, threatened Peter, {{ls}}aying, Goe behind me Satan, becau{{ls}}e thou {{ls}}auoure{{ls}}t not the things that are of God, but that are of men. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=34}} And calling the multitude<noinclude>{{rh|||together}}</noinclude>
